subject: ss-reproductive-medicine
title: Reproductive Medicine and Surgery
curriculum: Super-Speciality (DM/MCh / DrNB / FNB Reproductive Medicine and Surgery)
examPattern: NEET-SS Reproductive Medicine and Surgery Specialty Group paper (150 MCQs spanning hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrinology, folliculogenesis and spermatogenesis, comprehensive female and male infertility evaluation, ovulation induction and controlled ovarian stimulation, assisted reproductive technologies [IVF, ICSI, vitrification, PGT], embryology laboratory quality control, recurrent implantation failure and recurrent pregnancy loss, endometriosis and adenomyosis, PCOS, POI, Mullerian anomalies and reproductive surgeries, fertility preservation, and third-party reproduction / ethical-legal ART regulations).
book: Speroff's Clinical Gynecologic Endocrinology and Infertility 9th Edition; Yen & Jaffe's Reproductive Endocrinology 9th Edition; Gardner's Textbook of Assisted Reproductive Technologies 5th Edition; ESHRE Guidelines (PCOS, Endometriosis, POI, RPL, ART), ASRM Committee Opinions, and ART (Regulation) Act 2021 / Surrogacy Act 2021 India

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 2, Yen & Jaffe 9e Ch 1

mustKnow.fact: GnRH is synthesized by arcuate nucleus neurons and released in a pulsatile manner into the hypophyseal portal circulation with a physiological frequency of 60 to 90 minutes in the follicular phase and 180 to 240 minutes in the luteal phase.
Continuous unphysiological GnRH administration induces initial gonadotroph flare followed by receptor downregulation, internalization, and profound pituitary desensitization within 7 to 14 days.
Kisspeptin, neurokinin B, and dynorphin (KNDy) neurons in the arcuate nucleus act as the primary central pulse generator driving synchronized GnRH secretion.
FSH and LH share an identical 92-amino acid alpha subunit with TSH and hCG, but differ in their distinct beta subunits which confer hormone receptor specificity.
LH acts on ovarian theca cells via cAMP signaling to stimulate CYP11A1 and CYP17A1, converting cholesterol to androstenedione and testosterone.
FSH acts exclusively on ovarian granulosa cells to stimulate CYP19A1 (aromatase) expression, converting thecal androgens into estradiol.
Inhibin B is primarily secreted by small antral follicles under FSH stimulation and exerts selective negative feedback on pituitary FSH secretion.
The preovulatory LH surge is triggered when circulating estradiol levels exceed 200 pg/mL for at least 36 to 48 hours, switching estrogen feedback from negative to positive.

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 3, Yen & Jaffe 9e Ch 6

mustKnow.fact: The primordial-to-preovulatory follicle transition spans approximately 120 to 180 days, with the initial 85 days being gonadotropin-independent and governed by intraovarian paracrine factors.
Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) is produced by granulosa cells of primary, preantral, and small antral follicles (<8 mm) and inhibits excessive primordial follicle recruitment.
Dominant follicle selection occurs between days 5 and 7 of the menstrual cycle in the follicle possessing the highest density of FSH receptors and maximal intrafollicular estradiol.
Primary oocytes remain arrested in prophase of meiosis I (diplotene stage / dictyate) from fetal life until resumption triggered by the preovulatory LH surge.
The LH surge triggers resumption of meiosis I with extrusion of the first polar body, arresting the mature oocyte in metaphase of meiosis II (MII).
Ovulation occurs approximately 34 to 36 hours after the onset of the endogenous LH surge and 10 to 12 hours after the peak LH concentration.
Cumulus expansion during oocyte maturation requires oocyte-secreted factors GDF9 and BMP15 cooperating with hyaluronan synthesis mediated by HAS2.
Corpus luteum lifespan is tightly regulated to exactly 14 plus or minus 2 days in a non-pregnant cycle before undergoing luteolysis via endothelin-1 and PGF2-alpha.

topics.book: Campbell-Walsh 12e Ch 66, Yen & Jaffe 9e Ch 12

mustKnow.fact: Human spermatogenesis from spermatogonial stem cell division to mature spermatozoon requires approximately 64 to 74 days, followed by 10 to 14 days of epididymal transit.
Sertoli cells form the blood-testis barrier via tight junctions (claudin-11) between adjacent cells, segregating post-meiotic haploid germ cells from systemic circulation.
Leydig cells located in the testicular interstitium produce 95 percent of circulating testosterone under direct pulsatile LH stimulation acting on LH receptors.
Intratesticular testosterone concentration is 50 to 100-fold higher than systemic serum levels, maintained by androgen-binding protein (ABP) secreted by Sertoli cells.
Inhibin B and AMH are Sertoli cell markers reflecting seminiferous tubular function and spermatogenic reserve, exerting negative feedback on pituitary FSH.
Sperm capacitation in the female reproductive tract involves cholesterol efflux from the sperm plasma membrane, calcium influx via CatSper channels, and protein tyrosine phosphorylation.
Hyperactivation is a distinct vigorous whiplash-like flagellar motility pattern acquired during capacitation, essential for penetrating the cumulus oophorus and zona pellucida.
The acrosome reaction involves exocytotic fusion of the outer acrosomal membrane with sperm plasma membrane, releasing hyaluronidase and acrosin to digest the zona pellucida.

modules.name: Endometrial Receptivity and Window of Implantation

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 4, Yen & Jaffe 9e Ch 7

mustKnow.fact: The window of implantation is a discrete receptive period occurring between days 20 and 24 of an idealized 28-day cycle, corresponding to LH+7 to LH+9 (6 to 10 days post-ovulation).
Decidualization of endometrial stromal cells is driven by continuous progesterone and local cyclic AMP, characterized by expression of IGFBP-1 and prolactin.
Pinopodes (uterodomes) are apical cytoplasmic projections on luminal endometrial epithelial cells that peak during the mid-luteal implantation window.
The alpha-v-beta-3 integrin and mucin-1 (MUC1) modulation serve as classic molecular markers of the receptive endometrial luminal epithelium.
Uterine natural killer (uNK) cells constitute 70 percent of endometrial leukocytes in early pregnancy, possessing a CD56-bright CD16-negative phenotype that regulates trophoblast vascular remodeling.
Endometrial Receptivity Analysis (ERA) utilizes transcriptomic profiling of 238 genes to categorize endometrium as receptive, pre-receptive, or post-receptive.
Implantation proceeds through three sequential phases: apposition (unstable microvillar interdigitation), adhesion (stable integrin-mediated binding), and invasion (syncytiotrophoblast penetration).
Syncytiotrophoblast expresses non-classical HLA-G, HLA-E, and HLA-C to engage maternal decidual inhibitory receptors, evading maternal alloreactive immune destruction.

sections.name: Comprehensive Infertility Evaluation and Ovarian Reserve

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 27, ASRM Committee Opinion

mustKnow.fact: Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) serum levels exhibit minimal cycle-to-cycle and intra-cycle variation, making AMH the most reliable biochemical marker of functional ovarian reserve.
Serum AMH below 1.1 ng/mL indicates diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) and poor ovarian response in IVF, whereas AMH above 3.5 ng/mL signals high risk for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS).
Antral follicle count (AFC) is evaluated on cycle days 2 to 4 by counting all 2 to 10 mm follicles across both ovaries, with AFC under 5 to 7 defining low ovarian reserve.
Basal FSH above 10 IU/L on cycle day 2 or 3 signifies impaired negative feedback from waning follicle numbers, and FSH exceeding 20 IU/L strongly predicts poor stimulation yield.
Concomitant day 3 estradiol (E2) must be measured alongside FSH; an elevated basal E2 (>60 to 80 pg/mL) prematurely suppresses FSH into falsely normal ranges despite poor reserve.

The Bologna criteria for poor ovarian response require at least two of three features: advanced maternal age (>=40 years), previous poor response (<=3 oocytes with conventional protocol), or abnormal reserve (AFC <5-7 or AMH <0.5-1.1 ng/mL).
The POSEIDON criteria categorize patients with low prognosis in ART into four groups based on age, ovarian biomarkers (AMH/AFC), and prior ovarian response.
Ovarian reserve tests predict oocyte yield and gonadotropin response during stimulation, but do not predict natural fecundity or spontaneous pregnancy in fertile women.

modules.name: Tubal Patency and Uterine Cavity Evaluation

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 28, Ten Teachers Gyn 21e Ch 17

mustKnow.fact: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) is conventionally performed in the follicular phase between cycle days 7 and 10 following menstrual cessation, prior to ovulation.
HSG carries 65 percent sensitivity and 83 percent specificity for tubal occlusion, with oil-soluble contrast media showing significantly higher spontaneous pregnancy rates than water-soluble media.
Saline infusion sonohysterography (SIS) achieves superior diagnostic accuracy over HSG for intracavitary pathologies, distinguishing submucosal fibroids and endometrial polyps with >95% accuracy.
Hysterosalpingo-foam sonography (HyFoSy) allows real-time ambulatory tubal patency evaluation via transvaginal ultrasound without radiation or iodinated contrast.
Laparoscopy with chromopertubation using methylene blue or dilute indigo carmine remains the gold standard for diagnosing tubal patency, peritubal adhesions, and pelvic endometriosis.
Hydrosalpinx impairs IVF implantation by 50 percent and doubles miscarriage rates due to embryotoxic fluid reflux and mechanically flushing the uterine cavity.
Pre-IVF laparoscopic salpingectomy or proximal tubal clipping for hydrosalpinx significantly restores implantation and clinical pregnancy rates to baseline controls.
Hysteroscopy serves as the gold standard for definitive diagnosis and synchronous surgical correction of endometrial polyps, intrauterine synechiae (Asherman), and uterine septa.

modules.name: Semen Analysis (WHO 2021) and Sperm Function Tests

topics.book: WHO Laboratory Manual 6th Edition (2021), Campbell-Walsh 12e Ch 66

mustKnow.fact: WHO 6th Edition (2021) manual sets standard abstinence at 2 to 7 days, with semen sample collection delivered to laboratory and processed within 60 minutes at 37 degrees Celsius.
WHO 2021 lower fifth percentile reference limits are semen volume 1.4 mL, total sperm count 39 million per ejaculate, and sperm concentration 16 million/mL.
WHO 2021 motility reference limits establish total motility (progressive + non-progressive) at 42 percent and progressive motility (PR) at 30 percent.
Normal sperm morphology by Kruger strict criteria requires a minimum threshold of 4 percent morphologically normal spermatozoa with oval head and intact acrosome.
Sperm viability threshold is 54 percent live spermatozoa assessed by eosin-nigrosin exclusion or hypo-osmotic swelling (HOS) testing.
Leukocytospermia (pyospermia) is defined by peroxidase-positive leukocytes exceeding 1.0 million/mL in ejaculate, indicating genital tract inflammation or infection.
Sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI) exceeding 25 to 30 percent by TUNEL, Comet, or SCSA testing correlates with recurrent pregnancy loss, failed fertilization, and poor blastocyst formation.
Seminal fructose absence and acidic pH (<7.0) in an azoospermic ejaculate indicates bilateral congenital absence of vas deferens (CBAVD) or complete ejaculatory duct obstruction.

modules.name: Male Factor Infertility and Azoospermia Algorithms

topics.book: Campbell-Walsh 12e Ch 67, EAU Guidelines on Male Infertility

mustKnow.fact: Azoospermia requires verification on at least two centrifuged semen specimens (3000g for 15 minutes) revealing zero spermatozoa in the pellet.
Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) presents with elevated FSH, low or low-normal testicular volume (<15 mL), and testicular failure due to primary spermatogenic arrest or maturation arrest.
Obstructive azoospermia (OA) features normal testicular volume, normal serum FSH, distended epididymis, and mechanical blockage along the rete testis to ejaculatory ducts.
Microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) is the gold standard surgical sperm retrieval method for NOA, achieving sperm retrieval rates of 40 to 60 percent.
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) represents the commonest genetic etiology of NOA, characterized by small firm testes (<4 mL), hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, and tall eunuchoid habitus.
Y-chromosome microdeletions involve AZFa, AZFb, and AZFc regions: complete deletions of AZFa or AZFb indicate complete absence of sperm and contraindicate surgical retrieval (micro-TESE).
AZFc microdeletions (DAZ gene clusters) allow successful sperm retrieval via micro-TESE in 50 to 70 percent of cases, with mandatory transmission of the deletion to all male offspring.
Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD) is caused by CFTR gene mutations in over 70 to 80 percent of patients, mandating CFTR testing of both partners prior to ART.

sections.name: Ovulation Induction and Controlled Ovarian Stimulation

modules.name: Oral Ovulation Induction: Clomiphene and Letrozole

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 31, Legro et al PPCOS II (NEJM)

mustKnow.fact: Letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) is the first-line oral ovulation induction agent for anovulatory PCOS, demonstrating significantly higher live birth and ovulation rates compared to clomiphene.
Letrozole is initiated at 2.5 mg daily for 5 days starting on cycle days 2 to 5, titrating up to 5.0 mg and a maximum of 7.5 mg daily in resistant cycles.
Clomiphene citrate is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that blocks hypothalamic estrogen receptors, triggering endogenous GnRH and gonadotropin discharge.
Clomiphene anti-estrogenic effects on the cervix and endometrium produce thin endometrium (<7 mm) and hostile cervical mucus in 15 to 25 percent of treated patients.
Clomiphene resistance is defined by failure to ovulate after escalating doses up to 150 mg daily for 5 days across three consecutive cycles.
The multiple pregnancy rate with clomiphene citrate is approximately 5 to 8 percent (predominantly dizygotic twins), whereas letrozole carries a lower twin rate of 3 to 4 percent.
Adjuvant metformin (1500 to 2000 mg daily) improves insulin sensitivity, lowers circulating androgens, and increases ovulation rates in insulin-resistant clomiphene-resistant PCOS women.
Laparoscopic ovarian drilling (LOD) using 4 to 10 monopolar diathermy punctures (40W for 4 seconds) per ovary induces unifollicular ovulation without increasing multiple pregnancy or OHSS risk.

topics.book: Gardner ART 5e Ch 4, Speroff 9e Ch 32

mustKnow.fact: GnRH antagonist protocols (fixed day 6 or flexible lead follicle >=14 mm) have replaced long agonist protocols as the gold standard for high responders and PCOS, cutting OHSS by >50%.
GnRH antagonist protocols allow substitution of hCG with a GnRH agonist trigger (e.g., leuprolide 0.2 mg or triptorelin 0.2 mg) to virtually eliminate severe OHSS.

The classic long GnRH agonist protocol initiates mid-luteal pituitary downregulation (cycle day 21) for 10 to 14 days before starting exogenous gonadotropins upon achieving desensitization (E2 <50 pg/mL, no cysts).

Recombinant human FSH (follitropin alfa/beta) provides pure follicle-stimulating activity, whereas human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) provides 1:1 ratio of FSH and LH-like bioactivity derived from urinary hCG.
Microdose flare protocol utilizes initial GnRH agonist-induced endogenous gonadotropin discharge in low responders on cycle days 2 to 4 prior to initiating high-dose gonadotropins.
Premature LH surge in antagonist cycles is prevented by competitive blockade of pituitary GnRH receptors, with ganirelix or cetrorelix administered at 0.25 mg daily subcutaneous.
Final oocyte maturation trigger with recombinant hCG (250 mcg) or urinary hCG (5,000 to 10,000 IU) is timed when at least 2 to 3 follicles reach 17 to 18 mm in diameter.
Transvaginal ultrasound-guided oocyte retrieval (OPU) is scheduled exactly 35 to 36 hours post-trigger, immediately preceding natural follicular rupture.

topics.book: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 5, Speroff 9e Ch 32

mustKnow.fact: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) is driven by hCG-stimulated production of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) by hyperstimulated granulosa cells, increasing systemic capillary permeability.
Early OHSS occurs within 3 to 7 days post-trigger reflecting exogenous hCG response, whereas late OHSS develops 10 to 14 days post-trigger driven by endogenous trophoblastic hCG from pregnancy.
High-risk factors for OHSS include age <35 years, PCOS phenotype, AMH >3.5 ng/mL, AFC >20 to 24 follicles, and retrieving >18 to 20 oocytes.
Primary prevention of severe OHSS utilizes GnRH antagonist protocols combined with GnRH agonist trigger and elective whole-cohort blastocyst vitrification ('freeze-all' strategy).
Dopamine D2 receptor agonist cabergoline (0.5 mg daily for 8 days from trigger) prevents VEGFR-2 phosphorylation and significantly reduces hemoconcentration and ascites.
Severe OHSS is characterized by tense ascites, hydrothorax, hematocrit >45 percent, leukocytosis (>15,000/microL), oliguria, serum creatinine 1.1 to 1.5 mg/dL, and elevated liver enzymes.
Critical OHSS presents with tense ascites/hydrothorax, hematocrit >55 percent, anuria, acute kidney injury, thromboembolism, or acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).

Severe OHSS management demands strict fluid balance, crystalloid-first volume expansion with intravenous albumin (20%) for persistent hypoalbuminemia, and mandatory prophylactic low molecular weight heparin (LMWH).

topics.book: Gardner ART 5e Ch 6, ESHRE Guidelines on LPS

mustKnow.fact: Luteal phase defect is universal in stimulated IVF cycles due to supraphysiological steroid negative feedback suppressing pituitary LH and aspiration of thousands of granulosa cells during oocyte retrieval.
Luteal phase support is routinely initiated between evening of oocyte retrieval (OPU) and cycle day 3, with cessation recommended at 8 to 10 weeks of gestation when the luteoplacental shift occurs.
Micronized vaginal progesterone (400 mg twice daily or 8% gel 90 mg daily) achieves high local uterine tissue concentrations via the first uterine pass effect with minimal systemic side effects.

Oral dydrogesterone (10 mg two to three times daily) demonstrates equivalent live birth rates and superior patient tolerability compared to vaginal micronized progesterone in randomized trials (Lotus I and II).

In programmed/artificial frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles lacking a corpus luteum, intramuscular progesterone (50 to 100 mg daily) or combination therapies ensure adequate serum levels (>10 to 12 ng/mL).
Low serum progesterone (<8.8 to 10 ng/mL) on the day of embryo transfer in artificial FET cycles is associated with significantly reduced clinical pregnancy and elevated miscarriage rates.
hCG for luteal support significantly increases the risk of OHSS without improving pregnancy rates over progesterone alone, and is generally avoided.
Following GnRH agonist trigger in fresh transfer cycles, intensive luteal support requires either low-dose hCG rescue (1500 IU at OPU) or high-dose progesterone plus estradiol supplementation.

sections.name: Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) and Laboratory Procedures

modules.name: IVF vs ICSI and Gamete Micromanipulation

topics.book: Gardner ART 5e Ch 12 & 14

mustKnow.fact: Conventional IVF inseminates 50,000 to 100,000 progressively motile morphologically normal spermatozoa per oocyte in a microdrop under mineral oil.
Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) requires mechanical denudation of cumulus oophorus cells using hyaluronidase (80 IU/mL) to confirm oocyte maturity at metaphase II (MII).
ICSI injection is performed at the 3 o'clock position with the oocyte held by a holding pipette at 9 o'clock and polar body aligned at 6 or 12 o'clock to avoid disrupting the meiotic spindle.

Primary indications for ICSI comprise severe male factor infertility (severe oligoasthenoteratozoospermia, surgically retrieved epididymal/testicular sperm), prior fertilization failure in IVF, and preimplantation genetic testing.
Normal fertilization is confirmed 16 to 18 hours post-insemination/ICSI by the distinct presence of two clear pronuclei (2PN) and two polar bodies.
Physiological ICSI (PICSI) utilizes hyaluronic acid-coated plates to selectively bind mature spermatozoa with intact chromatin integrity and completed cytoplasmic maturation.
Intracytoplasmic morphologically selected sperm injection (IMSI) employs high-magnification differential interference contrast microscopy (>6000x) to detect sperm head vacuoles.
Oocyte activation deficiency after ICSI can be rescued by artificial oocyte activation (AOA) utilizing calcium ionophore (e.g., ionomycin, A23187) to induce cytosolic calcium oscillations.

modules.name: Embryo Culture, Gardner Grading and Vitrification

topics.book: Gardner ART 5e Ch 16 & 18

mustKnow.fact: Cleavage-stage embryo grading on day 3 assesses blastomere number (optimal 6 to 8 cells), symmetry, and percentage of extracellular fragmentation (<10% for Grade 1).
Gardner blastocyst grading evaluates blastocoel expansion (stages 1 to 6), inner cell mass (ICM, grades A/B/C), and trophectoderm (TE, grades A/B/C) on day 5 or 6.
Embryo genomic activation (maternal-to-zygotic transition) occurs at the 4-to-8 cell stage on day 3 in humans, governed by nascent embryonic transcription.
Sequential culture media mimic physiological oviductal fluid (low glucose, high pyruvate/lactate) for days 1 to 3 and uterine fluid (high glucose, essential amino acids) for days 3 to 5.
Time-lapse imaging (morphokinetics) uses closed-system incubation with built-in cameras to continuously track cleavage intervals (t2, t3, t5, cc2, s2) without ambient thermal stress.

Vitrification is an ultra-rapid cooling technique (>15,000 to 20,000 degrees C/min) using high concentrations of cryoprotectants that solidifies liquids into a glass-like state without intracellular ice crystallization.
Permeating cryoprotectants (dimethyl sulfoxide [DMSO], ethylene glycol) dehydrate intracellular water, while non-permeating cryoprotectants (sucrose, trehalose) exert extracellular osmotic drawing.
Post-thaw embryo survival rates following modern blastocyst vitrification exceed 95 percent, with live birth rates matching or exceeding fresh embryo transfers.

topics.book: Gardner ART 5e Ch 20, ASRM Committee Opinion on PGT

mustKnow.fact: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) tests all 24 chromosome pairs to detect whole or segmental aneuploidies using next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Trophectoderm biopsy at day 5 or 6 blastocyst stage biopsies 5 to 10 trophectoderm cells without compromising inner cell mass viability, achieving higher diagnostic reliability than day 3 blastomere biopsy.
PGT for monogenic/single-gene disorders (PGT-M) targets specific inherited mutations (e.g., cystic fibrosis, Huntington, thalassemia) using multiplex PCR and linkage analysis.
PGT for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) identifies unbalanced chromosomal products resulting from parental balanced reciprocal or Robertsonian translocations and inversions.

Embryonic mosaicism denotes the co-existence of two or more cytogenetically distinct cell lines, typically categorized as low-level (20% to 50% abnormal cells) or high-level (>50% abnormal cells) mosaicism.
Parental carrier screening prior to PGT-M requires molecular workup of affected probands or grandparents to establish haplotype phase and eliminate allele dropout (ADO) false negatives.
Non-invasive PGT (niPGT) analyzes cell-free embryonic DNA (cfDNA) spent in the blastocyst culture droplet, avoiding physical cellular micromanipulation.
PGT does not replace prenatal diagnostic confirmation: chorionic villus sampling (CVS) or amniocentesis remains recommended in all PGT-achieved pregnancies.

modules.name: IVF Laboratory Quality Control and Air Quality

topics.book: Gardner ART 5e Ch 2, ESHRE Revised Guidelines for Good Practice in IVF Labs

mustKnow.fact: IVF laboratory cleanroom air must comply with ISO Class 7 (Class 10,000) or ISO Class 8 standards, while working areas inside laminar flow workstations must achieve ISO Class 5 (Class 100).

Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and chemical airborne contaminants are toxic to mammalian embryo cleavage and require multi-stage carbon and potassium permanganate filtration alongside HEPA filters.
Trigas benchtop incubators utilize physiological low oxygen tension (5 percent O2, 6 percent CO2, 89 percent N2), significantly reducing oxidative stress compared to atmospheric 20 percent oxygen.
Extracellular pH of culture media must be maintained within a strict physiological range of 7.25 to 7.35 by equilibrium against exact ambient incubator CO2 concentration.

Temperature control requires continuous calibration to 37.0 degrees Celsius (+/- 0.2 C), as brief transient drops below 35 C induce irreversible meiotic spindle depolymerization in metaphase II oocytes.
Embryo culture media osmolality must be tightly controlled between 270 and 290 mOsm/kg, shielded from evaporative hyperosmolality by mineral oil overlay.
Witnessing and identification systems (electronic RFID/barcode tracking or double witness) are mandatory at every gamete transfer, denudation, injection, cryopreservation, and warming step.
Liquid nitrogen storage tanks for cryopreserved gametes and embryos must feature continuous continuous telemetry temperature logging and vacuum failure alarm monitors.

sections.name: Implantation Failure, Pregnancy Loss and Endometriosis

topics.book: ESHRE Working Group on RIF, Yen & Jaffe 9e Ch 24

mustKnow.fact: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) is currently defined by ESHRE as failure to achieve clinical pregnancy after transfer of at least 3 euploid blastocysts or >=4 good-quality cleavage embryos.
Chronic endometritis is found in 15 to 30 percent of RIF cases, definitively diagnosed by identifying syndecan-1 (CD138) positive stromal plasma cells on endometrial biopsy.
First-line therapy for CD138-positive chronic endometritis is oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days, achieving mucosal histological cure rates of >80%.
Endometrial scratch injury performed in the preceding luteal phase has been demonstrated by large multicenter randomized trials to confer no significant benefit in live birth rates in unselected RIF.
Displacement of the receptive window occurs in approximately 20 to 25 percent of RIF patients, amenable to personalized embryo transfer (pET) guided by endometrial transcriptomic profiling.
Intrauterine infusion of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF, 300 mcg) or platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is utilized experimentally for refractory thin endometrium (<7 mm) in RIF.
Subclinical hydrosalpinx missed on routine 2D ultrasound must be aggressively evaluated with HSG or laparoscopy and removed or clipped prior to subsequent embryo transfers.
Immunotherapy add-ons (intravenous intralipid, prednisone, IVIG) currently lack high-level evidence from randomized controlled trials to support routine clinical recommendation in RIF.

topics.book: ESHRE Guideline on RPL (2022 Update), ASRM Committee Opinion

mustKnow.fact: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is defined by ESHRE as the spontaneous loss of two or more pregnancies, which does not require consecutive losses.
Parental peripheral blood karyotyping detects balanced reciprocal or Robertsonian translocations in 3 to 5 percent of couples with RPL, warranting genetic counseling and PGT-SR.

Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is the most treatable secondary etiology of RPL, requiring at least one laboratory criterion (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgG/IgM >40 GPL/MPL, anti-beta-2-glycoprotein-1) confirmed 12 weeks apart.

Obstetric APS in pregnancy is treated with low-dose aspirin (75 to 100 mg daily) combined with prophylactic low molecular weight heparin (LMWH), initiated upon pregnancy confirmation and continued through delivery.
Septate uterus is the commonest congenital uterine anomaly linked to RPL and second-trimester miscarriages, due to poor vascularity of the fibroelastic fibrous septum.
Endocrine screening for RPL comprises thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH target <2.5 mIU/L), anti-TPO antibodies, HbA1c, and serum prolactin.
Microarray or next-generation sequencing for copy number variants on products of conception (POC) identifies embryonic aneuploidy as the underlying cause in >50% of sporadic and RPL losses.
In unexplained RPL, supportive care in a dedicated recurrent miscarriage clinic achieves a subsequent successful live birth rate of 70 to 75 percent without empirical interventions.

topics.book: ESHRE Guideline Endometriosis (2022), Ten Teachers Gyn 21e Ch 15

mustKnow.fact: Endometriosis affects 30 to 50 percent of women presenting with infertility, impairing fecundity via peritoneal chronic inflammation, pelvic adhesions, and reduced oocyte quality.

The revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine (rASRM) classification scores endometriosis into Stage I (minimal, 1-5), Stage II (mild, 6-15), Stage III (moderate, 16-40), and Stage IV (severe, >40).
Endometrioma cystectomy stripping damages healthy adjacent ovarian cortex and significantly depletes ovarian reserve, lowering serum AMH by an average of 30 to 40 percent.
Laparoscopic cystectomy for endometriomas >=4 cm prior to IVF does not improve IVF pregnancy rates or live births and should be reserved for severe pain or suspicious features.
Pre-treatment with GnRH agonists for 3 to 6 months prior to fresh or frozen embryo transfer improves clinical pregnancy rates in women with stage III/IV endometriosis and adenomyosis.
Adenomyosis presents with asymmetric myometrial thickening, subendometrial microcysts, and junctional zone (JZ) maximal thickness exceeding 12 mm on MRI or transvaginal ultrasound.
Endometriosis Fertility Index (EFI) validated from 0 to 10 reliably predicts spontaneous conception probabilities over 36 months following surgical staging of endometriosis.

Deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) involving bowel or bladder requires multidisciplinary surgical excision for intractable pain, but IVF is preferred over extensive surgery when infertility is the primary indication.

modules.name: PCOS Phenotypes and Premature Ovarian Insufficiency (POI)

topics.book: International PCOS Guideline (2023), ESHRE POI Guideline

mustKnow.fact: International PCOS Guideline (2023) Rotterdam consensus requires 2 of 3 criteria: ovulatory dysfunction, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM).
Ultrasound PCOM diagnostic criteria (2023) require follicle number per ovary (FNPO) >=20 (using transducer >=8 MHz) in either ovary or ovarian volume >=10 mL, in the absence of corpora lutea.
Serum AMH can now be utilized for defining PCOM in adults according to 2023 International PCOS guidelines, substituting for transvaginal ultrasound.
Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is defined by amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea for >=4 months before age 40, with elevated FSH >25 IU/L on two occasions at least 4 to 6 weeks apart.
Genetic etiology in POI accounts for 10 to 20 percent of cases, mandating peripheral blood karyotyping (Turner mosaicism 45,X) and FMR1 premutation testing (55 to 200 CGG repeats).
Autoimmune POI requires screening for 21-hydroxylase adrenal antibodies (anti-21OH) and thyroid peroxidase antibodies (anti-TPO) to rule out polyglandular autoimmune syndromes.
Spontaneous conception occurs in 5 to 10 percent of women with idiopathic POI due to intermittent, unpredictable resumption of follicular activity.
Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) with transdermal 17-beta estradiol (100 mcg patch) and cyclic natural progesterone is mandatory in POI until the average age of natural menopause (age 50 to 52).

sections.name: Reproductive Surgeries, Fertility Preservation and ART Regulations

topics.book: ASRM 2021 Mullerian Anomalies Classification, Ten Teachers Gyn 21e Ch 6

mustKnow.fact: The ASRM 2021 Mullerian anomaly classification system categorizes uterine malformations into Mullerian agenesis, cervical agenesis, unicornuate, uterine didelphys, bicornuate, septate, and arcuate.

Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome represents 46,XX Mullerian agenesis with congenital absence of uterus and upper two-thirds of vagina, while ovarian function and secondary sex characteristics are completely normal.

Distinction between septate uterus and bicornuate uterus is established by fundal external contour on 3D ultrasound or MRI: external fundal indentation >1 cm defines bicornuate, while <1 cm or flat/convex contour confirms septate uterus.
Hysteroscopic metroplasty with cold scissors or unipolar/bipolar needle electrode without touching the myometrium is the surgical treatment of choice for symptomatic uterine septum.
Strassman metroplasty (fundal unified wedge resection) is reserved strictly for symptomatic bicornuate uterus causing repetitive mid-trimester fetal loss, never for septate uterus.

Asherman syndrome (intrauterine synechiae) staging (ESGE) guides hysteroscopic adhesiolysis, followed by postoperative placement of pediatric Foley catheter or intrauterine stent and high-dose estradiol (4 to 6 mg daily for 30 days).
Intramural uterine fibroids distorting the endometrial cavity (FIGO Type 2) or submucosal fibroids (FIGO Types 0 and 1) impair implantation and warrant surgical myomectomy prior to ART.
Laparoscopic tubal reanastomosis (isthmic-isthmic) for reversed tubal sterilization achieves cumulative pregnancy rates of 65 to 75 percent in women aged <35 years with >4 cm residual tube.

topics.book: ASRM Committee Opinion Fertility Preservation, Yen & Jaffe 9e Ch 26

mustKnow.fact: Oocyte vitrification (mature metaphase II oocytes) is an established, non-experimental standard of care for female fertility preservation prior to gonadotoxic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation.
Random-start controlled ovarian stimulation allows initiating gonadotropins in the late follicular or luteal phase without awaiting menstruation, avoiding cancer chemotherapy delays.

In estrogen-sensitive malignancies (hormone receptor-positive breast cancer), co-administration of letrozole (5 mg daily) during ovarian stimulation safely suppresses circulating estradiol while maintaining oocyte yields.

Ovarian tissue cryopreservation (OTC) is the only fertility preservation option for prepubertal girls, involving laparoscopic cortical biopsy/oophorectomy and slow freezing or vitrification of cortical strips.
Orthotopic ovarian tissue transplantation onto the remaining ovary or peritoneal pelvic sidewall restores endocrine function in >90% of cases and has resulted in hundreds of healthy live births.
Ovarian transposition (oophoropexy) translocates ovaries laterally and cranially out of the planned radiation field, preserving gonadal function in >80% undergoing pelvic radiotherapy.

Sperm cryopreservation through masturbatory ejaculation or surgical retrieval prior to initiating cancer therapies is the first-line and highly effective fertility preservation strategy for adolescent and adult males.
Gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (GnRHa) co-treatment during chemotherapy provides ovarian protection against cyclophosphamide-induced POI in premenopausal breast cancer patients.

modules.name: Third-Party ART, Surrogacy and Indian ART Act 2021

topics.book: The ART (Regulation) Act 2021 India, The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021 India

mustKnow.fact: The ART (Regulation) Act 2021 of India defines permissible age limits for ART services as 21 to 50 years for females and 21 to 55 years for males.

Under the Indian ART Act 2021, an oocyte donor must be an ever-married woman aged 23 to 35 years with at least one living child of her own (minimum 3 years old), donating oocytes only once in her lifetime.
Sperm donor age under Indian regulations is restricted to 21 to 55 years, and a semen donor can donate to only one ART bank and supply semen to only one commissioning couple or woman.

Commercial surrogacy is completely prohibited in India under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021, allowing only altruistic gestational surrogacy with an Essentiality Certificate issued by the appropriate board.

Surrogate mother eligibility criteria require a married woman aged 25 to 35 years having a child of her own, acting as a surrogate only once in her life, with no monetary remuneration except medical and insurance expenses.
The ART Act 2021 restricts the maximum number of embryos transferred into a woman's uterus during an ART cycle to no more than three, with elective single embryo transfer (eSET) strongly encouraged.
Mandatory health insurance for oocyte donors (12 months) and surrogate mothers (36 months) covering postpartum complications is legally mandated under Indian law.
Sex selection or preimplantation sex determination for non-medical reasons is strictly illegal and punishable under the PC-PNDT Act 1994 and ART Act 2021.

modules.name: Complications in ART: Ectopic, Heterotopic and Long-Term Outcomes

topics.book: Speroff 9e Ch 32, Gardner ART 5e Ch 24

mustKnow.fact: Heterotopic pregnancy (coexistent intrauterine and ectopic pregnancy) incidence rises from 1 in 30,000 in spontaneous conceptions to approximately 1 in 100 to 1 in 500 in ART cycles.
Ectopic pregnancy occurs in 1.5 to 3 percent of all clinical IVF pregnancies, predominantly located in the ampulla or interstitial/cornual segment of the fallopian tube.
Oocyte retrieval complications include pelvic infection (0.5%), severe hemoperitoneum due to iliac or ovarian vessel injury (0.1%), and ureteral or bowel perforation.
Elective single embryo transfer (eSET) decreases multiple gestation rates from >25 percent to <2 percent while preserving cumulative live birth rates across frozen cycles.

Frozen embryo transfer (FET) is associated with reduced risks of low birth weight, preterm birth, and small-for-gestational-age compared to fresh transfers, but carries an increased risk of large-for-gestational-age (LGA) and maternal hypertensive disorders.

Monozygotic twinning occurs in 1.5 to 2.5 percent of blastocyst transfers, approximately 2 to 3-fold higher than in cleavage-stage transfers, hypothesized to arise from inner cell mass splitting during extended culture or zona manipulation.
Long-term epidemiological studies confirm that ovulation-inducing drugs and IVF do not increase the invasive risks of ovarian, breast, or endometrial cancer.

Imprinting disorders (Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, Angelman syndrome, Silver-Russell syndrome) exhibit a modest relative increase in children conceived via ART, associated with epigenetic alterations during in vitro embryo culture.
